strings.d1.s0.name: Kiyomizu-dera
strings.d1.s0.tips: Wooden terrace built without a single nail; empty at 08:00. Try the three streams of Otowa waterfall, and look out for the spring and autumn night openings.
strings.d1.s1.name: Sannenzaka & Ninenzaka
strings.d1.s1.tips: Preserved stone-stepped lanes; stop at the tatami-floored Starbucks and sample yatsuhashi (cinnamon sweets).
strings.d1.s2.name: Kodai-ji
strings.d1.s2.tips: Zen garden and bamboo grove; the temple of Hideyoshi's widow.
strings.d1.s3.name: Nishiki Market
strings.d1.s3.tips: "Kyoto's Kitchen", a 400-year-old market: tamagoyaki (rolled omelette), yuba (tofu skin) and pickles. No eating while walking. Allow for 2 streets.
strings.d1.s4.name: Gion Hanamikoji
strings.d1.s4.tips: The geisha district: Shirakawa canal, and between 17:30 and 18:00 the maiko head to work. Follow the photo rules; private lanes are off limits.
strings.d1.b0.name: Omen Nishiki
strings.d1.b1.name: Yasaka Shrine
strings.d1.b1.tips: Gion's shrine and Maruyama Park; lanterns glow at night.
strings.d2.s0.name: Fushimi Inari Taisha
strings.d2.s0.tips: 10,000 red torii gates; empty at 07:00. It's 45 minutes to the Yotsutsuji viewpoint (2.5 hours for the full loop). Open 24 hours.
strings.d2.s1.name: Byodo-in Uji
strings.d2.s1.tips: The Phoenix Hall from the 10 yen coin; 15 minutes on the JR Nara line, museum included.
strings.d2.s2.name: Nakamura Tokichi Uji
strings.d2.s2.tips: A tea house since 1854: matcha soba and parfait, expect a queue, and try the Uji matcha tasting.
strings.d2.s3.name: Uji River & Ujigami Shrine
strings.d2.s3.tips: Japan's oldest shrine and the riverbank; tea shops along the way.
strings.d2.s4.name: Fushimi Sake District Gekkeikan
strings.d2.s4.tips: Sake breweries along the canal; the Gekkeikan Okura Museum includes 3 tastings.
strings.d2.b0.name: Tofuku-ji
strings.d2.b0.tips: Zen garden and the Tsutenkyo bridge (autumn); an alternative to Uji.
strings.d2.b1.name: Tsuen Tea Uji
strings.d2.b1.tips: The world's oldest tea house, since 1160; at the foot of the bridge.
strings.d3.s0.name: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove
strings.d3.s0.tips: A corridor of bamboo; crowded after 08:00, so enter through Tenryu-ji's north gate.
strings.d3.s1.name: Tenryu-ji
strings.d3.s1.tips: UNESCO-listed Zen temple; Sogenchi garden with its borrowed mountain scenery.
strings.d3.s2.name: Togetsukyo Bridge & Katsura River
strings.d3.s2.tips: The "Moon Crossing Bridge"; boat rides and hills of cherry and maple.
strings.d3.s3.name: Arashiyama Yoshimura Soba
strings.d3.s3.tips: Soba with a view of the bridge; tempura too.
strings.d3.s4.name: Iwatayama Monkey Park
strings.d3.s4.tips: Macaque monkeys on the mountaintop; a 20-minute climb with city views.
strings.d3.b0.name: Sagano Romantic Train
strings.d3.b0.tips: Train through the Hozugawa valley; Torokko Saga, an alternative to the monkeys (stunning in autumn).
strings.d3.b1.name: % Arabica Arashiyama
strings.d3.b1.tips: Coffee on the riverbank; expect a queue.
strings.d4.s0.name: Kinkaku-ji
strings.d4.s0.tips: The Golden Pavilion; opens at 09:00, reflected in the pond. The loop takes 30 minutes.
strings.d4.s1.name: Ryoan-ji
strings.d4.s1.tips: Zen garden of 15 stones; sit quietly and you'll only see 14 of them.
strings.d4.s2.name: Ninna-ji
strings.d4.s2.tips: Five-storey pagoda and the late-blooming Omuro cherry trees (April).
strings.d4.s3.name: Nijo Castle
strings.d4.s3.tips: The shogun's palace; the "nightingale floors" squeak, plus the Ninomaru garden. Closed Tuesdays in some months.
strings.d4.s4.name: Honke Owariya
strings.d4.b0.name: Ippudo Nishiki
strings.d4.b1.name: Kyoto Imperial Palace
strings.d4.b1.tips: The imperial palace; free, an alternative to Nijo (closed Mondays).
strings.d5.s0.name: Nara Park Deer
strings.d5.s0.tips: 35 minutes on the Kintetsu line (direct from Kyoto); 1,200 free-roaming deer, shika senbei (deer crackers) cost 200 yen, and the deer will bow to you.
strings.d5.s1.name: Todai-ji Daibutsu
strings.d5.s1.tips: A 15 m bronze Buddha in the world's largest wooden building; try squeezing through the pillar hole.
strings.d5.s2.name: Kasuga Taisha
strings.d5.s2.tips: A path lined with 3,000 stone lanterns, set in the forest.
strings.d5.s3.name: Nakatanidou Mochi
strings.d5.s3.tips: Lightning-fast mochi pounding show; try the yomogi (mugwort) mochi.
strings.d5.s4.name: Naramachi
strings.d5.s4.tips: Old merchant quarter; the Koshi-no-ie house and cafes.
strings.d5.b0.name: Kamameshi Shizuka Nara
strings.d5.b0.tips: Rice cooked in an iron pot (kamameshi); next to the park.
strings.d5.b1.name: Isuien Garden
strings.d5.b1.tips: A garden that borrows Todai-ji as its backdrop; an alternative to Naramachi.
strings.d6.s0.name: Ginkaku-ji
strings.d6.s0.tips: The Silver Pavilion (it isn't actually silver); sand cone and moss garden.
strings.d6.s1.name: Philosopher's Path
strings.d6.s1.tips: A 2 km canal path: cherry blossom in April, maples in November, and cats.
strings.d6.s2.name: Nanzen-ji
strings.d6.s2.tips: The Suirokaku aqueduct and Sanmon gate; Tenjuan garden.
strings.d6.s3.name: Okutan Nanzenji Yudofu
strings.d6.s3.tips: Simmered tofu (yudofu) beside the temple; open since 1635, with a quiet garden.
strings.d6.s4.name: Heian Shrine
strings.d6.s4.tips: Giant red torii; the garden has weeping cherries in April.
strings.d6.b0.name: Blue Bottle Kyoto Nanzenji
strings.d6.b0.tips: Coffee in a machiya (traditional townhouse); an alternative to the tofu.
strings.d6.b1.name: Kyoto National Museum
strings.d6.b1.tips: National treasures; a rainy-day alternative to Heian Shrine.
strings.d7.theme: Pontocho morning and a gentle farewell
strings.d7.s0.name: Kamo River Morning Walk
strings.d7.s0.tips: Along the riverbank; stepping stones between Sanjo and Shijo, and herons.
strings.d7.s1.name: Pontocho Alley
strings.d7.s1.tips: A narrow geisha lane, quiet by day; kawayuka terraces in the evening (May to September).
strings.d7.s2.name: Kyoto Station Isetan
strings.d7.s2.tips: Inside the station: a depachika (basement food hall) and yatsuhashi souvenirs; the rooftop Skyway is free.
strings.d7.s3.name: Kyoto Ramen Koji
strings.d7.s3.tips: 8 regional ramen shops on the station's 10th floor; a fitting farewell.
strings.d7.s4.name: Kyoto Station Haruka Kansai
strings.d7.s4.tips: The Haruka express takes 75 minutes to Kansai; the bus to Itami takes 55 minutes.
strings.d7.b0.name: Kyoto Tower Sando
strings.d7.b1.name: To-ji
strings.d7.b1.tips: Japan's tallest pagoda, next to the station; flea market on the 21st of each month.
strings.note0: The bus costs 700 JPY a day (tourist routes are packed); metro plus bus is 1,100. ICOCA is the most practical option. Haruka from Kansai takes 75 minutes; JR from Osaka takes 30 minutes. Bike rental is 1,000 a day.
strings.note1: Summer brings 33-36°C and humidity (Gion Matsuri on 17 July, Daimonji on 16 August); June means rain and hydrangeas; kawayuka river terraces; set out at 7 am.
strings.note2: Temples cost 500-800 JPY in cash; no eating while walking in Nishiki; private lanes in Gion have been off limits since 2024, and don't stop maiko.
strings.note3: Yudofu, kaiseki (10,000+), obanzai (Kyoto home cooking), matcha; ramen 1,000, teishoku (set meal) 1,200; no tipping, cards are becoming more common but carry cash.
strings.note4: Kiyomizu, Fushimi and the Bamboo Grove before 08:00; Kinkaku-ji and Nara open at 09:00; check Nijo's closing days.
strings.note5: Nara's deer eat paper and will bow; when the senbei is gone, show them your empty hands.
strings.transit.name: ICOCA + daily bus
strings.transit.why_chosen: Kyoto's bus network is extensive; the metro has only 2 lines; ICOCA works everywhere
